sections.title: Introduction: The Intuitive Hook
lecture_lines: Can a square fit inside any loop?
This is the famous Inscribed Square Problem.
We call these loops Jordan Curves.
animations: Fade in title: 'Introduction: The Intuitive Hook' using color #FFFFFF.
Animate two points in 2D space moving towards each other.
Draw a line segment connecting the two points.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Configuration Space
lecture_lines: We define squares by center and size.
This maps to a 3D configuration space.
The space connects back to the loop.
animations: Fade in title: 'Prerequisite: The Configuration Space' using color #FFFFFF.
Show a square plane representing possible point configurations.
Highlight a diagonal constraint line inside the square plane.

sections.title: The Mathematical Mechanism: Symmetry & Topology
lecture_lines: It relates spheres and flat planes.
Opposite points must have matching values.
This forces a square to emerge.
The topology guarantees a solution exists.
animations: Fade in title: 'The Mathematical Mechanism: Symmetry & Topology' using color #FFFFFF.
Display a circular symmetry group rotating on screen.
Deform a square into a triangle to show topological invariance.
Use color #FF4500 to highlight intersection points of paths.
Finalize the graph structure with nodes labeled #00CED1.

sections.title: Visualizing the Inscription
lecture_lines: Visualize a square template sliding along.
Rotate and shrink the square carefully.
A square is now fully inscribed.
animations: Fade in title: 'Visualizing the Inscription' using color #FFFFFF.
Animate a shape rotating inside another fixed boundary shape.
Use color #FFD700 to trace the path of the inner shape.
Flash the final inscribed geometric configuration.
Show the overlap region filling with color #32CD32.

sections.title: Conclusion & Generalizations
animations: Fade in title: 'Conclusion & Generalizations' using color #FFFFFF.

Fade out all elements one by one for conclusion.
